title: Check yourself: Tools, arguments, forked skills and the practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A skill's header lists `allowed-tools: Read Grep`, and its author expects editing to be impossible while the skill is active. What actually happens?

options.text: Editing is removed from the available tools until the next message
options.says: Ruled out because removal belongs to the other field, which removes tools "from Claude's available pool while this skill is active".

options.text: Editing is refused because only the two listed tools are permitted
options.says: Ruled out because the field "does not restrict which tools are available: every tool remains callable".

options.text: Editing runs without any prompt because the skill vouches for it
options.says: Ruled out because "your permission settings still govern tools that are not listed".

options.text: Changing files remains allowed under the usual permission settings
options.says: The field pre-approves and restricts nothing.

origin.section: Tools, arguments, forked skills and the practice

questions.stem: A skill's text says only 'Use these naming conventions for new endpoints', and its header sets `context: fork`. What does the isolated helper do?

options.text: It reads the whole conversation and applies the conventions to it
options.says: Ruled out because the helper "doesn't see your conversation history".

options.text: It gets guidelines but no assignment, and returns nothing useful
options.says: A forked skill's body is its prompt, and guidelines without a task give the helper nothing to do.

options.text: It asks the user which endpoint the conventions concern
options.says: Ruled out because the helper starts from the skill text alone, which "gives it the skill content as its prompt", so it has no one to ask.

options.text: It runs inside the main conversation as if nothing were forked
options.says: Ruled out because the setting "starts a new subagent of the type named in" the agent field, so it does not stay in the conversation.
